The Book of Joy

By: Michael Duffett | Production

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
Archbishop Desmond Tutu, despite ailing health, recently celebrated his 85th Birthday. Last month a book called the Book of Joy was published which is an intimate look into conversations between two of the worlds most prominent spiritual leaders, Desmond Tutu and the Dalai Lama. In 2015, the author of the book, Archbishop Tutu travelled to the Dalai Lama's home in India to celebrate his 80th birthday. The book offers a rare opportunity to experience their astonishing and unprecedented week together.

Together with the book is the Share the Joy campaign led by the Archbishop and the Dalai Lama. These two men who have known great suffering are hoping to show and spread the message that joy and compassion will always win. The campaign is hoping to reach millions to share, create and experience joy.

Press Release:


Tutu talks Joy
In a world suffering turmoil, war, famine and more, is it still possible to find a sense of joyfulness? Carte Blanche reports on a week-long conversation between friends, confidantes and winners of the Nobel Peace Prize, His Holiness the Dalai Lama and Archbishop Desmond Tutu. The product? Their advice for living with joy.


Script:


SCRIPT

DESMOND TUTU:
You don’t wake up in the morning and say, “Hey, I’m going to call my friend to the Dalai Lama.” It just happens.

Two world icons, two Nobel peace prize laureates, Arch bishop Desmond Tutuand his holiness the Dalai Lama came together last year in India. The occasions was the Dalai Lama’s 80 birthday but it was much more than that – they were there to create a gift for others, the book of joy.,,,,,on lasting happiness in a changing world.

And On the 7th of October it was the Arch’s 85th birthday. 100’s of well wishers gathered at St. George’s Cathedral in cape town to share the Eucharist and celebrate the occasion with him.

Present at the birthday celebration was the co author of the book of joy, Douglas Abrahams who presented the arch with a copy.

DOUG:  The Archbishop is exactly as he seems. He’s the real deal, and he’s really in many ways the most human human I’ve ever met.

Doug first heard the arch when he was student at an American university.

DOUG:
When I was in college it was the time of the anti-apartheid struggle and the divestment movement in the US, and he came to lecture at our university. And at that time he was a towering presence and an incredible inspiration.

He never imagined then that years later he would become the arche’s literary agent, The idea for the book of joy was borne when Doug attended the archbishops wife’s leah’s birthday celebration 3 years ago in cape town. Also there was the chairman of the Dalai Lama foundation.

DOUG:  And he said, “How about these two guys writing a book together?” And we both looked at each other and we said “What would it be on?” and we said, “Joy.” These are two of the most joyous people on the planet and so we turned to Archbishop Tutu and we said, “Do you want to write a book with the Dalai Lama?” And he said, “Yeah, I’d do anything with that man!” So we were off and running.

JOHN:
The Book of Joy chronicles a weeklong conversation between two of the biggest spiritual icons of our time. In it they draw on their own experiences to help answer the question: how do we fill our own lives with joy?

Despite ailing health in April last year the arch travelled to Daramsala in india where the Dalai Lami lives in exile. Their affection for each other was obvious. The Arch’s. Daughter Reverend Canon Mpho Tutu- van Furth accompanied her dad.

MPHO TUTU-VAN FURTH:
The closest analogy I could find for my father and the Dalai Lama together on the whole is two eight-year-old boys in Ms. Smith’s class, and they have a real playful click. They keep enjoining each other and then telling each other, “Ok, now you have to act holy.”

DESMOND TUTU:  You see, he’s not not listening.

DALAI LAMA:
I will not listen.

DESMOND TUTU:  Shhh. Behave like a holy man.

JOHN:  One of the conundrums this book speaks to is how, if are experiencing suffering or seeing suffering in others, we’re able to fill our lives with joy?

Both men have experience oppression and hardship in their lives. They say that’s its because of this that it’s because of this they have been able to cultivate joy i. It was doug’s task to interview them for a 5 day period.

DOUG:  What the Dalai Lama and the Archbishop were saying is that it’s not to deny any of those realities to want to cultivate more joy in your life, but to actually face that suffering, recognize that suffering, honor that suffering, is actually part of the path of experiencing more joy.

They identify 8 pillars of joy that can then be achieved. They also said that joy is in fact our birthright and even more fundamental that happiness.

Reverend canon Mpho tutu van furth adds that personal suffering can be so great that professional help should be considered.

MPHO TUTU-VAN FURTH
When you are in that state of depression, absolutely get professional help. It is available, you don’t have to kind of charge through it on your own. But beyond that psychological care, actually turning your attention outside yourself can be an incredible resource for building joy.

JOHN:
While both men are religious, one being Buddhist and the other a Christian, they were adamant that this book shouldn’t be a religious text and that there should be a significant contribution from science.

DOUG:  They were wanting this to be a human book. And they really wanted to find out what was at the heart of their shared humanity, and not just what is Buddhist and what is Christian.

DESMOND TUTU:  People innately are good, you know.

DALAI LAMA: All have sort of desire to have happy life, happy day, happy month.

DOUG:
The Dalai Lama is very clear on what he calls “secular ethics.” He appeals I think a lot to atheists and people with no religion because really what they’re going for is the heart of being human.

Thee culmination of the week was the birthday celebration for the dlamalami. because he is a monk, he has never danced before. In typical mischievous fashion the arch was not having none of that.

JOHN:
Amongst your father’s many achievements, one of the most extraordinary perhaps was getting the Dalai Lama to dance.

MPHO TUTU-VAN FURTH
He didn’t actually kind of get down and boogie, but he did—I saw a sway!

Back in cape town, youth handed out cup cakes to strangers to celebrate the arches birthday and to bring attention to to the hashtag share the joy campaign.

DOUG:  The #Sharethejoy campaign and the Joy Experiments were inspired by the Book of Joy, where people wanted to take the message of the book, which is fundamentally this idea that the more joy we bring to others, the more we experience joy, and to actually bring it out into the world.

social media platforms are being set up to reach the widest audience possible.

JOHN:  The project is inspired by the Book of Joy, but am I right in saying that it’s also inspired by a need to kick back against the prevailing atmosphere of the world?
ALYSSA:  Absolutely. We really believe that the world needs a joy movement now more than ever, and especially having the wisdom of the Dalai Lama and the Archbishop, we were just so inspired by everything that came out of the book that we couldn’t help but do something about it in the wider world.

Available here, the book is already on best seller lists in many countries. It will be a lasting legacy of two giants who now approach their own mortality, often with humour... At his birthday the arch said that he was closer to the departure than the arrivals hall. .

DOUG:  They were so funny while they were together. They were joking and the Archbishop Tutu said, “Well you don’t have to worry so much,” to the Dalai Lama, “because of the reincarnation.” And then the Dalai Lama joked back and said, “Well actually, with reincarnation that’s a lot of uncertainty. You know you’re going to heaven.” So it was very funny. They were laughing the whole week together.

For Doug those 5 days in India were life-changing.

DOUG:  Getting to be with these two extraordinary icons of joy and of well-being, and to be able to have them to share with one another what I think is their wealth spring of joy and vitality, it really felt like it was a mountaintop experience.
